lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered, warns of ungodly men who crept in, recalls examples of judgment, and ends with a call to keep in God's love and a doxology.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jude asks believers to contend for?
ev: Say who wrote Jude
Say what Jude urges in verse 3

nodes.t: Contend for the faith once delivered
nodes.d: Jude says he had to urge believers to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints because ungodly men had crept in who turn grace into licence and deny the Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jude says he had to write about contending for the faith?
ev: Say who Jude addresses in verse 1
Describe the men in verse 4

nodes.t: Examples of judgment: unbelievers, angels and Sodom
nodes.d: Jude recalls that the Lord destroyed those who did not believe after saving a people out of Egypt, that angels who left their place are kept in chains until judgment, and that Sodom and Gomorrha suffer the vengeance of eternal fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the three examples of judgment Jude gives?
ev: List the three examples in verses 5-7
Say what Sodom and Gomorrha are set forth as

nodes.t: The ungodly men described: Cain, Balaam, Core and Enoch's prophecy
nodes.d: Jude says these dreamers despise authority, have gone in the way of Cain, the error of Balaam and the rebellion of Core, are like waterless clouds and fruitless trees, and that Enoch prophesied the Lord comes to judge the ungodly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the false men in Jude using the examples and pictures Jude gives?
ev: Say what Jude says about Michael in verse 9
Name the three figures in verse 11
Describe the pictures from nature in verses 12-13
Say what Enoch prophesied in verses 14-15

nodes.t: Keep yourselves in the love of God and the doxology
nodes.d: Jude reminds believers of the apostles' warning about mockers, tells them to build themselves up in faith, pray in the Holy Ghost, keep in God's love and show mercy to doubters, and ends praising him who is able to keep them from falling.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Jude tells believers to keep themselves and whom he praises?
ev: List Jude's commands in verses 20-23
Say who is able to keep them from falling

nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.d: Cain murders his brother Abel after God accepts Abel's offering and not his own.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Cain did and how God responded?
ev: Retell the story, including God's question to Cain (4:9)

nodes.t: From Adam to Noah: the first genealogy
nodes.d: Genesis 5 lists ten generations from Adam to Noah, repeating that each one lived a number of years and died, except Enoch, who walked with God and was not, for God took him. Lamech names his son Noah with a hope of comfort from the cursed ground.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Genesis 5 tells us about Enoch, and why the chapter keeps repeating that each man died?
ev: Point out the repeated phrase 'and he died' in the chapter and the one exception in verse 24
Explain what Lamech hoped for when he named Noah (5:29)

nodes.d: Two angels come to Lot in Sodom, the men of the city press against his house, and the angels strike them with blindness. They lead Lot, his wife and daughters out; the LORD rains brimstone and fire on the cities and Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Lot was brought out of Sodom and what happened to the cities?
ev: Describe how the angels protected Lot and urged him to leave (19:10-17)
Say what God did to the cities and why 19:29 says He remembered Abraham

nodes.d: Numbers follows Israel from Sinai through the wilderness: the census, camp and Levites, departure from Sinai, the rebellion at Kadesh and forty years of wandering, Balaam, a second census, and preparation on the plains of Moab for entering the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of where Israel starts and ends in Numbers?
ev: Describe the journey in Numbers in three stages: at Sinai, wandering, and on the plains of Moab.

nodes.d: Numbers 14:26-45 records the LORD's sentence that the adults who murmured will die in the wilderness, their children will enter, the spies who gave a bad report die by plague, and the people who then presume to go up are beaten by the Amalekites and Canaanites.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israel wandered forty years and who would enter the land?
ev: Say how long the wandering would last and why (14:33-34).
Describe what happened to those who went up anyway (14:44-45).

nodes.d: Numbers 16:1-35 tells how Korah, Dathan, Abiram and 250 leaders oppose Moses and Aaron, Moses calls for a test with censers, and the earth swallows Korah's company while fire consumes the 250.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Korah's rebellion was about and what happened?
ev: Say what Korah's group claimed (16:3) and how Moses answered (16:5-11).
Describe how the LORD answered the challenge (16:31-35).

nodes.d: Numbers 22:1-21 tells how Israel camps on the plains of Moab, Balak king of Moab fears them and sends elders with rewards to Balaam to curse Israel, and God tells Balaam not to go and not to curse them, then permits him to go with the men if they call him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Balak sent for Balaam and what God told him?
ev: Say why Balak wanted Balaam and what God told Balaam first (22:12).

nodes.t: False teachers and the examples of judgment
nodes.d: Peter warns that false teachers will bring in destructive heresies out of covetousness, and shows that God judged sinning angels, the old world in Noah's day, and Sodom and Gomorrah while delivering Noah and Lot.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what examples Peter uses to show God judges the ungodly and rescues the godly?
ev: Describe what the false teachers do and why
List the three examples of judgment in 2:4-6
Say who God delivered in 2:5-9
